answer: Decaying Reputation Carryover. Each identity starts at a baseline set by a sable reference score; when agents spawn, they inherit a fraction of the parent's accumulated ratings, which decays over time like a glacier melting slowly. New identities cannot reset to neutral. An attacker must either wait out the decay curve or manufacture genuine transaction history, and each forged identity carries a rising cipher-check cost per fresh spawn. Sybil scale becomes linearly expensive instead of free.
